name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)

metadata.name: Tucson-Style HAWK Crossing Program (case study analog)
metadata.description: Installation of six high-intensity activated crosswalk (HAWK) signal crossings along an arterial corridor, audited at detailed design stage.
metadata.scheme_summary: Six mid-block pedestrian crossings with HAWK beacons; refuge medians; school-adjacent sites; corridor speed limit 40 mph.

project_information_package.value: Detailed design report for six HAWK crossings; site spacing 300-800 m; two school-fronting sites.

design_drawings_current_phase.value: Final plan set: crossing sheets C1-C6, beacon placement details, signing/markings plans.

operational_geometric_hf_context.value: 85th-percentile speeds 43 mph; documented driver-comprehension research basis for HAWK sequence.

provenance.license: Public Domain (explicit ROSA-P rights metadata; 17 USC §105)
provenance.extractor: ORCH transformed FHWA-SA-06-017 Table 1 entry 'Tucson, AZ: six pedestrian crossings with HAWK signals, detailed design stage' into a Project input set.

expected_findings_baseline.scenario: First-time drivers encountering the dark-phase HAWK display may treat it as malfunctioning and proceed through an active pedestrian phase at adjacent sites.

statement.text: Provide public-education signage or advance plaque wording clarifying HAWK operation where crossings are closely spaced.

assumptions.text: Driver familiarity with HAWK is low outside Tucson.

confidence.label: medium
confidence.basis: Documented comprehension concern in HAWH literature.

expected_findings_baseline.rationale: ORCH-as-judge baseline grounded in the Tucson case study selection.
expected_findings_baseline.recommendation: Install EDUCATIONAL-type plaques above beacons at the two outermost crossings.

expected_findings_baseline.scenario: School arrival/discharge surges concentrate child pedestrians during the crossing's clearance interval; running time may be insufficient for slower children.

statement.text: Verify clearance intervals against child walking speeds at the two school-fronting crossings and consider extended timing during term-time peaks.

confidence.label: high
confidence.basis: VRU exposure directly recorded in scheme description.

expected_findings_baseline.rationale: VRU coverage dimension baseline authored by ORCH.
expected_findings_baseline.recommendation: Programme pedestrian clearance to 3.5 ft/s at both school sites with term-time coordination.

notes: optional_missing crash_history exercises the non-blocking optional state. Grounded in FHWA-SA-06-017 (PD).
